notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in the story: date of the fall (16/17 April 1851), date of first lighting of the stone tower (15 Nov vs 18 Nov 1860), tower height (89, 97, 102 ft 9 in). The USLHS place record lists the original optic as third-order Fresnel (1860) and a tower height of 85 ft; the 1894 Light-House Board report and LighthouseFriends say the 1894 Mahan lens was second-order, and the 1935 Bulletin says the present lens is second-order. Not resolved in the story beyond saying the lens was second-order in 1894; the 1860 lens order is not stated. Keeper Bennett is Joshua in the 1851 Worcester Spy and John W. in the roster. The Spy of 18 April 1851 quotes the Collector's note dated 17 April, so 'yesterday' (tower seen standing near 4 p.m.) is read as Wednesday 16 April; the paper's 'Wilson aged 20' follows its OCR. The Dunham journal quotation is from LighthouseFriends (second-hand). Milton Reamy's Bulletin obituary says he retired 1 Jan 1919 from the service; the roster ends his Minots head-keeper stint in 1915, consistent with 28 years at the ledge. The Tornberg dory episode and Octavius Reamy's 1917 capsizing rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The 1894 report's page numbers (233-234, 240) were read from the OCR page heads; the 1899 passage is cited by scan page 88. Roster matched by the tool; no OCR-table matching by column position was needed. Not examined: 1894 lens-installation details in a primary source; Official Registers. Checker 2026-10-27: Bulletin 1935 and LighthouseFriends give 16 April 1851 for the fall, Swift gives about 1 a.m. 17 April; the story now states both. Current ownership of the tower after the 2014 auction was not verified beyond the Globe and Lighthouse Digest.
